Title: Software Engineer, Platform Experience
Description: Meet Siena Siena is the Agent of Record for consumer brands. One agent that owns the entire customer journey, running on a shared intelligence layer no point tool can replicate. Consumer brands run ten or more disconnected tools to manage their customers. We collapse that stack into a single agent. It started with support, the hardest surface a brand has, and it expands from there: Shopping Agent, Social Agent, Siena working alongside a brand's own operators. One agent across every surface, with shared memory, shared context, and shared tools. Hundreds of brands already run real customer volume on Siena in production. This is built, working, and growing, and we are racing to build what comes next. The team We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do. We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock. If you want to own real problems rather than close tickets, keep reading. The role You take the hardest problems our customers hit in production and solve them end to end. A webhook that stopped firing overnight. An agent filling the wrong parameter. A report that won't reconcile. Today those land on a product engineer's desk and pull them off the roadmap. That stops with you. More than troubleshooting. You find the real cause, work the customer directly to a resolution (including jumping on a call when that's fastest), then build the automation so it never comes back. You're an accelerator. Every fix makes the next one faster and the product better. A clear path forward. This is the front door to deployment and platform work at Siena. Grow from here into a Forward Deployed Engineer or deeper into platform engineering. Who you are You solve problems end to end. Given a customer, some logs, and a vague symptom, you find the break and tell a customer-side cause from a product bug. You don't stop at "it's not our bug." You like talking to customers. You'll get on a call, find the real problem behind the report, and resolve it live. Customer contact is leverage, not a chore. You're excited to build automation. The fix in front of you is half the job. Building the thing that means nobody fixes it again is the other half. You think in leverage. This is the signal that matters most. You're fluent with AI agents and prompts. You've built or debugged LLM workflows and know how they break: prompts, knowledge bases, intent classification, retrieval, and the gap between what passes in test and what runs live. You can read a prompt, spot why it misfires, and rewrite it. No black boxes. You read and reason through code. You're comfortable in our core stack — Node.js, TypeScript, React, Express — or close enough to ramp fast. You can trace customer-side JavaScript in the browser, write diagnostic SQL against PostgreSQL, and navigate a backend service without waiting on someone else. You use AI coding tools as leverage. Fluent with Claude Code or equivalent to script a query, clean a dataset, or navigate a new codebase fast. Judgment about when to automate, not syntax recall. You own problems nobody assigned you. You've worked where the process didn't exist yet, found something broken, and driven it to a fix. You make people around you better. You leave teammates more capable through docs, tools, and walkthroughs. Nice to have: observability tooling (Grafana, Honeycomb, Sentry); internal tooling that turned manual work into a system. Ecommerce or DTC exposure is a plus, not a requirement. What you'll do Own the hard problems end to end. Trace, reproduce, fix, or hand engineering a clean reproduction. Range across APIs and integrations, customer-side JavaScript, agent behaviour, and data. Get on the call when that's the fastest path. Debug the agents and the prompts. Diagnose whether a wrong answer or misfire is prompt, knowledge base, config, or model, then fix the prompt or setup so it holds under real traffic. Build so it doesn't happen twice. For every fix, two questions you own: can the team handle this next time with a runbook or tool, and what do we build so the system catches the next one. This half compounds. Close the loop to Product. You're the structured, metrics-backed signal between what customers hit in the wild and what we build next. Surface patterns, not one-offs. Make the product measurably better. Raise the team's floor. Lift what the whole team can resolve instead of being the only one who can. Know where your scope ends. Escalate genuine product bugs, infra, and outages with a clean reproduction, not a shrug. What success looks like The point of this role isn't closing tickets faster. It's that the product visibly gets better because you've killed the root cause of recurring problems. Resolution is the floor. Product quality is the win. By 90 days: you've named the top recurring failure patterns and you're attacking them at the root, not patching symptoms. At least one class of problem is fixed in the product itself, not just resolved ticket by ticket, so it stops showing up at all. Resolution is handled without pulling engineers off the roadmap, but the real signal is fewer problems existing in the first place. By 6 months: recurring issue classes are measurably down because the root causes are gone, the product is demonstrably more robust, and your feedback loop to Product is shipping real improvements. The team resolves more on its own because the system catches the next one, not heroics. Why Siena? Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox. Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast. A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in. A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one. Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build. Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we. AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster. Our values The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback—both giving and receiving it—because they care more about getting things right than being polite. They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward. Our approach to AI The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem. Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows. At Siena, we’re not just looking for people who can do a job. We’re looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that’s you, we look forward to your application. We use AI-assisted screening tools as part of our hiring process. All decisions are made by humans. You can request a human-only review at talent@siena.cx. Siena provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Title: Java Coding Specialist - Freelance AI Trainer Project
Description: Java Coding Specialist - Freelance AI Trainer Project United States of America Are you a Java expert who can spot a flawed abstraction from across a codebase? Large-scale language models are evolving from clever chatbots into engines of real scientific and engineering progress. High-quality training data is what separates a capable model from a genuinely useful one. That data starts with people who actually know the craft. We're looking for Java specialists with deep fluency in object-oriented design, concurrency, JVM internals, data structures, algorithms, and system architecture. You'll put advanced language models through their paces on Java problems spanning a wide range of difficulty and complexity, assessing whether model-generated solutions are correct, well-reasoned, and production-quality. That means evaluating not just whether code runs, but whether it's the right approach, whether edge cases are handled, and whether the reasoning behind it holds up. You'll review Java problems and model-generated solutions, judge correctness and code quality, identify where the model's logic breaks down, and document failure patterns clearly enough that others can act on them. You may also flag whether a given problem is well-specified and appropriately challenging for training purposes. A bachelor's, master's, or PhD in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field is a strong signal. So is real-world Java experience, competitive programming, open-source contributions, or technical writing. The ability to clearly articulate why a solution is wrong or weak, not just that it is, matters as much as the technical depth. Ready to put your Java expertise to work shaping the next generation of AI? Apply today. We offer a pay of $45 per hour for candidates who successfully pass our preliminary Java-focused assessments. As a contractor, you'll supply your own secure computer and high-speed internet. Company-sponsored benefits such as health insurance and PTO do not apply. Project Type: Freelance / Contract Workplace type: Remote

Title: Research Analyst - Oil Monitoring Refining

Main Responsibilities We are looking for an Analyst to work as part of our Research team covering our Trading Analytics segment . Analyse asset and market developments for the commodities they cover, generating forecasts on what will happen in the short-term and the long-term. Connect and build relationships with clients to inform their analysis and strategies. Collaborate with colleagues covering other sectors to generate an integrated view of the Energy and Natural Resources sector. Write insightful commentary on the challenges and opportunities for the commodities they cover, specifically around the Energy Transition, Oil-Petrochemical integration, and the drive towards Sustainability. Support efforts to improve current internal processes. Research and data gathering – we identify and gather intelligence that feeds our industry expertise. We need inquisitive and passionate people with a keen eye for detail. Analysis - we provide market-leading research using this data/intelligence and form opinions for, and tell stories to, our customers. We need people with natural curiosity with the potential to become experts in their field and with the ability to articulate – both verbally and in writing – clear, insightful analysis. Your existing knowledge will enhance our coverage as you develop your career. Keen interest in commodity market dynamics - as someone with a keen interest in commodity market dynamics, you want to understand how these markets impact the natural resources industry and our everyday lives. Analytical mindset and eye for detail - your analytical mindset and attention to detail have been honed through academic and/or work experience. You're comfortable collecting and interpreting data, articulating your findings clearly, and seeking to enhance your knowledge by asking thoughtful questions. You have experience with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, which helps you present your findings in a visually compelling way. Highly adaptive team player - you thrive in fast-paced environments and are excited about the opportunity to work cross-functionally on a variety of tasks. You can work independently or as part of a team, generating ideas and striving to be the best in class. Excellent communication skills - Your strong command of English, both written and spoken, allows you to communicate effectively in the globalised commodity market. Fluency in an additional language would be advantageous. Expectations Growth mindset - taking the initiative to learn new skills, seeking out feedback and coaching, and actively applying what has been learned in the workplace. Change agility - maintaining high performance through disruption and change. Title: LATAM FF Impact Analyst
Description: Viatris Healthcare México S. de R.L. de C.V Viatris is a global healthcare company uniquely positioned to bridge the traditional divide between generics and brands, combining the best of both to more holistically address healthcare needs globally. With a mission to empower people worldwide to live healthier at every stage of life, we provide access at scale, currently supplying high-quality medicines to approximately 1 billion patients around the world annually and touching all of life's moments, from birth to the end of life, acute conditions to chronic diseases. We have been included on number of award lists that demonstrate the impact we are making. Every day, we rise to the challenge to make a difference and here is how the LATAM FF Impact Analyst role will make an impact: The LATAM FF Impact Analyst is responsible for measuring, monitoring, and optimizing the return on investment (ROI) of medical visits and all promotional support provided to healthcare professionals (HCPs) across LATAM. This role ensures that field force activities, sampling strategies, medical support initiatives, and other promotional investments generate measurable business impact while strictly adhering to compliance standards and corporate governance policies. The position plays a critical role in elevating LATAM’s analytical maturity by linking activity, investment, and outcomes, enabling data-driven decision-making and reinforcing ethical and compliant promotional practices across the region. Key responsibilities for this role include: Field Force Impact & ROI Monitoring Design and implement frameworks to measure ROI of medical visits, sampling, and promotional investments across markets. Develop activity-to-impact models linking call frequency, segmentation, sampling, and commercial outcomes (Rx, sales, DDD). Monitor field force productivity and effectiveness indicators across clusters Identify performance gaps, threats, and growth opportunities through advanced analytics. Provide regular impact assessments to regional and country leadership teams. Standardize impact measurement methodologies across markets. Embed ROI and impact insights into governance routines and business reviews. Evaluate the effectiveness of medical samples, promotional materials, events, and other HCP support initiatives. Develop standardized metrics and dashboards to monitor promotional investment performance. Support resource reallocation decisions based on ROI and impact analysis. Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner closely with Sales, Marketing, and Country Leadership teams. Support incentive design by ensuring alignment between investment, activity, and measurable outcomes. Coordinate with Global teams to align methodologies and best practices. Success Indicators Clear and measurable linkage between field force activity and business outcomes. Improved ROI of medical visits and promotional investments across LATAM. Standardized regional impact measurement framework. Increased analytical maturity and data-driven decision-making within the organization. Qualifications for this role are: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Data Analytics, Life Sciences, or related field. 2-3 years of experience in Business Analytics, Sales Force Effectiveness, Commercial Excellence, or similar roles within pharmaceuticals or healthcare. Strong experience in ROI analysis, performance analytics, and CRM data interpretation. Experience working in multi-country or regional environments preferred. Professional proficiency in English and Spanish; Portuguese is a strong plus. Skills/Requirements Strong analytical and quantitative skills. Ability to translate data into actionable business insights. High integrity and strong compliance mindset. Structured, detail-oriented, and results-driven. Strong stakeholder management and communication skills. Ability to operate in a cross-functional environment. At Viatris, we offer competitive salaries, benefits and an inclusive environment where you can use your experiences, perspectives and skills to help make an impact on the lives of others. Viatris is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
